title: Multiple Myeloma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison); regimen leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by id, and the dose engine computes patient doses. No proprietary guideline text reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated.

a.text: Myeloma-defining events (any one, with clonal marrow plasma cells): CRAB features (hyperCalcemia, Renal insufficiency, Anemia, lytic Bone lesions) OR a SLiM biomarker (clonal plasma cells >=60%, involved:uninvolved serum free light-chain ratio >=100, or >1 focal MRI lesion).

b.text: R-ISS integrates ISS stage (beta-2-microglobulin, albumin) with serum LDH and high-risk FISH; used here for prognosis, not to withhold therapy.

c.text: High-risk cytogenetics by FISH: t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), del(17p), and gain/amplification of 1q21. Presence of >=2 abnormalities is often termed double-hit disease.

d.text: Supportive care is concurrent, not optional: bone-modifying agent (zoledronic acid or denosumab), VTE prophylaxis while on an immunomodulatory drug, herpes-zoster prophylaxis with a proteasome inhibitor or anti-CD38 antibody, and infection/vaccination review.

nodes.name: Plasma-cell disorder
nodes.title: Plasma-cell disorder / disease phase
nodes.description: Select the plasma-cell disorder category or disease phase to route the pathway.
bullets: MGUS (monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance)
Smoldering (asymptomatic) multiple myeloma
Active (symptomatic) newly diagnosed multiple myeloma
Relapsed or refractory disease after prior therapy

nodes.name: MGUS workup
nodes.title: MGUS: workup
nodes.description: Confirm a small clone with no end-organ damage and stratify progression risk.
bullets: SPEP with immunofixation and serum free light chains; quantitate the M-protein
CBC, calcium, creatinine to exclude CRAB
Marrow biopsy and imaging only if intermediate/high-risk or unexplained CRAB
Risk factors: non-IgG isotype, M-protein >=1.5 g/dL, abnormal free light-chain ratio

nodes.name: MGUS: observe
nodes.title: MGUS: observation, no treatment
nodes.description: No treatment; periodic monitoring for progression.
bullets: No cytotoxic therapy - MGUS is precursor, not cancer
Recheck M-protein and CRAB labs at 6 months, then every 1-2 years by risk
Re-evaluate promptly for new anemia, bone pain, renal change or rising M-protein

nodes.name: Smoldering workup
nodes.title: Smoldering myeloma: workup
nodes.description: Confirm marrow clone and M-protein burden without myeloma-defining events.
bullets: Marrow biopsy for clonal plasma-cell percentage and FISH
SPEP/UPEP with immunofixation, serum free light chains
Whole-body low-dose CT or PET/MRI to exclude lytic lesions and focal marrow disease
Confirm absence of CRAB and SLiM biomarkers

nodes.name: Smoldering risk
nodes.title: Smoldering myeloma: progression risk (20/2/20)
nodes.description: Stratify 2-year progression risk to decide observation versus early therapy or trial.

nodes.name: SMM low: observe
nodes.title: Smoldering, lower risk: observation
nodes.description: Active surveillance without therapy.
bullets: No treatment outside a trial - overall survival benefit of early therapy is unproven at lower risk
M-protein and CRAB labs every 3-6 months
Repeat marrow and imaging on biochemical change

nodes.name: SMM high: trial / lenalidomide
nodes.title: Smoldering, high risk: clinical trial or lenalidomide
nodes.description: Consider early intervention to delay progression; trial preferred.
bullets: Clinical trial is the preferred pathway for high-risk smoldering disease
Off trial, single-agent lenalidomide can delay progression to active myeloma
Close monitoring; treat as active myeloma once a myeloma-defining event appears

nodes.name: NDMM workup
nodes.title: Newly diagnosed MM: workup checklist
nodes.description: Establish diagnosis, tumor burden, cytogenetics and organ status before therapy.
bullets: CBC, calcium, creatinine, albumin, LDH, beta-2-microglobulin
SPEP/UPEP with immunofixation, serum free light chains, 24h urine
Marrow aspirate/biopsy with FISH panel (del17p, t(4;14), t(14;16), 1q)
Whole-body imaging: low-dose CT, or PET/CT or whole-body MRI
Assess performance status, comorbidity and transplant candidacy

nodes.name: Myeloma-defining events
nodes.title: Confirm active disease (CRAB / SLiM)
nodes.description: A myeloma-defining event distinguishes active myeloma from smoldering disease.
bullets: CRAB: hyperCalcemia, Renal insufficiency, Anemia, lytic Bone lesions
SLiM: >=60% clonal plasma cells, FLC ratio >=100, or >1 focal MRI lesion

options.label: No defining event - reclassify as smoldering

nodes.name: R-ISS stage
nodes.title: Staging: Revised International Staging System
nodes.description: Assign R-ISS for prognosis; does not change the decision to treat.

tables.title: R-ISS staging
rows: ISS I (B2M < 3.5 and albumin >= 3.5) AND normal LDH AND no high-risk FISH
ISS III (B2M >= 5.5) AND (high LDH OR high-risk FISH)

nodes.name: Cytogenetic risk
nodes.title: Risk stratification: FISH cytogenetics
nodes.description: High-risk cytogenetics favor sustained/intensified therapy and inform prognosis.

tables.title: Cytogenetic risk (FISH)
rows: Hyperdiploidy, t(11;14), t(6;14); none of the high-risk lesions

nodes.name: Supportive care
nodes.title: Concurrent supportive care
nodes.description: Start alongside anti-myeloma therapy, not after it.
bullets: Bone-modifying agent: zoledronic acid or denosumab (denosumab if renal impairment)
VTE prophylaxis (aspirin or anticoagulant) with any immunomodulatory drug
Herpes-zoster prophylaxis with a proteasome inhibitor or anti-CD38 antibody
Renal protection: hydration, avoid nephrotoxins; treat hypercalcemia
Vaccination and infection review

nodes.name: Transplant eligibility
nodes.title: Autologous transplant candidacy
nodes.description: Candidacy is driven by physiologic fitness, organ function and comorbidity, not a rigid age cutoff.

nodes.name: TE induction
nodes.title: Transplant-eligible: induction
nodes.description: Triplet or quadruplet induction to maximal response before stem-cell collection.
bullets: Quadruplet Dara-VRd (daratumumab + bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone) deepens response, favored especially for high-risk disease
Triplet VRd (bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone) is an accepted backbone
Give 3-4 cycles, then proceed to stem-cell collection
Avoid prolonged lenalidomide before collection to protect stem-cell yield

nodes.name: ASCT
nodes.title: Stem-cell collection and autologous transplant
nodes.description: High-dose melphalan with autologous rescue after induction response.
bullets: Mobilize and collect stem cells (store enough for a possible second transplant)
High-dose melphalan conditioning followed by autologous stem-cell infusion
Early transplant deepens response and prolongs progression-free survival
Delayed transplant (collect now, transplant at first relapse) is an option in selected standard-risk patients

nodes.name: TE maintenance
nodes.title: Post-transplant maintenance
nodes.description: Continuous maintenance after transplant prolongs remission.
bullets: Lenalidomide maintenance until progression is standard
For high-risk cytogenetics, add a proteasome inhibitor (bortezomib or carfilzomib) to maintenance
Monitor blood counts and for second primary malignancy

nodes.name: TI induction
nodes.title: Transplant-ineligible: induction
nodes.description: Continuous triplet therapy adapted to frailty.
bullets: Dara-Rd (daratumumab + lenalidomide + dexamethasone) continuous therapy is a preferred option
VRd-lite (attenuated bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone) suits frailer or neuropathy-prone patients
Weekly subcutaneous bortezomib dosing and dexamethasone dose-reduction lower toxicity in older patients
Adjust doses to frailty; treat continuously to progression

nodes.name: TI maintenance
nodes.title: Transplant-ineligible: continued therapy
nodes.description: Continue the active backbone to progression.
bullets: Continue lenalidomide (with or without daratumumab) as maintenance/continuous therapy
De-escalate dexamethasone after the first cycles to reduce toxicity
Reassess frailty and tolerance at each cycle

nodes.name: Response / MRD
nodes.title: Response assessment (IMWG) and MRD
nodes.description: Grade depth of response; MRD is prognostic.

tables.title: IMWG response categories
rows: CR plus normal FLC ratio and no clonal marrow plasma cells
No clone at >= 10^-5 by NGS or flow

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance on therapy
nodes.description: Serial monitoring to detect relapse early.

tables.title: Monitoring schedule
rows: CBC, calcium, creatinine, SPEP, serum free light chains
For new symptoms or biochemical progression

nodes.name: Continued surveillance
nodes.title: Sustained response: continue maintenance and monitoring
nodes.description: Ongoing maintenance with scheduled monitoring.
bullets: Continue maintenance to progression or intolerance
Keep serial M-protein and free light-chain trends
Re-enter the relapse pathway on confirmed progression

nodes.name: Relapse workup
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory: restaging
nodes.description: Confirm relapse and re-characterize disease before selecting next-line therapy.
bullets: Confirm IMWG progression (rising M-protein/FLC, new CRAB, or new lesions)
Repeat marrow with FISH to detect clonal evolution (e.g., new del17p, t(11;14))
Whole-body imaging for new bone or extramedullary disease
Catalog prior drug exposure and refractoriness (last regimen, best response, time to relapse)

nodes.name: Relapse stratification
nodes.title: Next line by prior exposure / refractoriness
nodes.description: Choose a regimen that does not repeat a drug the disease is refractory to; introduce a new class.

nodes.name: KRd
nodes.title: Lenalidomide-sensitive relapse: KRd
nodes.description: Carfilzomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone.
bullets: KRd (carfilzomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone) for lenalidomide-sensitive relapse
Baseline and on-treatment cardiac assessment (carfilzomib cardiotoxicity)
Daratumumab-based lenalidomide triplets are an alternative if anti-CD38-naive

nodes.name: DPd
nodes.title: Lenalidomide-refractory relapse: DPd
nodes.description: Daratumumab + pomalidomide + dexamethasone.
bullets: Pomalidomide + dexamethasone backbone with an anti-CD38 antibody (daratumumab or isatuximab)
Switches both the immunomodulatory drug (to pomalidomide) and adds a new class
VTE prophylaxis and herpes-zoster prophylaxis

nodes.name: Triple-refractory options
nodes.title: Triple-class exposed: immunotherapy choice
nodes.description: Select a BCMA/GPRC5D-directed immunotherapy by access, fitness and logistics.

nodes.name: BCMA CAR-T
nodes.title: Triple-class exposed: BCMA CAR-T
nodes.description: Autologous BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy.
bullets: One-time BCMA CAR T-cell product (idecabtagene or ciltacabtagene) after >= prior lines
Needs apheresis and manufacturing time; use bridging therapy if disease is fast-moving
Monitor for cytokine-release syndrome and neurotoxicity at a certified center
No StewardMD dose protocol - cellular therapy, not a computed regimen

nodes.name: Bispecific
nodes.title: Triple-class exposed: bispecific antibody
nodes.description: Off-the-shelf T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody.
bullets: BCMA-directed (teclistamab, elranatamab) or GPRC5D-directed (talquetamab)
Step-up dosing with inpatient monitoring for cytokine-release syndrome
Infection prophylaxis and immunoglobulin support; continuous dosing to progression
No StewardMD dose protocol - step-up schedule per product label

nodes.name: Belantamab
nodes.title: Triple-class exposed: belantamab mafodotin
nodes.description: BCMA antibody-drug conjugate.
bullets: BCMA-directed antibody-drug conjugate, often combined with pomalidomide or bortezomib
Mandatory ophthalmology monitoring for keratopathy; dose-modify for ocular toxicity
Option where CAR-T or bispecifics are inaccessible
No StewardMD dose protocol - ocular-risk program applies

nodes.name: Venetoclax
nodes.title: t(11;14): venetoclax-based therapy
nodes.description: BCL2 inhibitor for t(11;14) relapse.
bullets: Venetoclax (with dexamethasone or bortezomib) is active in t(11;14) or BCL2-high disease
Restrict to t(11;14)-positive relapse; benefit is biomarker-defined and off-label
Watch for infection risk; monitor counts
No StewardMD dose protocol - biomarker-restricted use

nodes.name: Salvage ASCT
nodes.title: Salvage autologous transplant
nodes.description: Second autologous transplant after a durable first remission.
bullets: Consider if first remission was durable (roughly >= 36 months on maintenance) and the patient is fit
Reinduction to response, then high-dose melphalan with stored or re-collected stem cells
Follow with maintenance; otherwise pursue a novel-class regimen
No StewardMD dose protocol - conditioning per transplant unit
